authority: operator 2026-10-18: 'a script with rules that's repeatable, n8n should run this weekly; and also monitor when a threshold is over 80%, fix and move to n8n where monitored.' Readers: scripts/disk_hygiene.py (rules A), scripts/disk_usage_monitor.py (monitor B), scripts/tmp_hygiene.py (tmp, operator 2026-10-19 after the /tmp inode incident). Packet docs/ops/packets/disk-hygiene-n8n-20261018/. Changed only by reviewed PR.
_paths: '~' expands to the running user's home. Every threshold, path and keep-count lives here; the scripts hold no defaults of their own beyond refusing to run without this file.

protected_paths._why: Never a candidate under any rule: the dev repo (cron and units execute from it), the release-prep clone, the served release pointers. A candidate equal to, inside, or containing one of these is excluded.

never_touch._why: HARD list, enforced in code before any rule runs and again at apply time. A path equal to / inside one of `paths`, with a path component in `names`, or with a name matching `name_globs` is never a candidate. `report_only` paths are measured and printed, never deleted.

report_only.why: cache root, report only unless a cache rule is enabled
npm cache root, report only unless a cache rule is enabled

git._why: Rule G: a linked worktree or standalone clone is a candidate ONLY if every check passes (scripts/disk_hygiene.py evaluate_git). Linked worktrees are removed with `git -C <main repo> worktree remove <path>` (never --force, never rm -rf); standalone clones are removed only under the same checks.

releases._why: Rule R: keep the CURRENT target, every pointer-file target, the previous served release (newest older than CURRENT by name timestamp), and the newest `keep_newest`. `hold_until` honours an archive's own tripwire README (no candidate before that date).

roots.hold_reason: archive/releases_20260915/README_TRIPWIRE.md: 'Delete after 2026-12-14 (90 days) unless something here is still needed' (operator approved 2026-09-15)

caches._why: Rule C: optional, default disabled. An entry `item_depth` levels under `path` whose newest mtime is older than `older_than_days` is a candidate.

references._why: A candidate whose absolute path appears in any of these texts is excluded (crontab, systemd units and drop-ins, release pointer files).

apply._why: --apply needs a manifest written within `manifest_max_age_hours`, a non-empty TRADEAI_DISK_HYGIENE_GRANT (the env name is fixed in code so the n8n env allowlist can be checked statically), and re-validates every item; it stops at the caps. Never runs under the n8n executor (TRADEAI_RUN_ID set): AGENTS.md §23.14 keeps destructive retention off n8n.

tmp._why: Incident 2026-10-19 ~13:40 ET: /tmp (tmpfs, 1,048,576 inodes) hit 97% INODES with 20G bytes free; ended Claude sessions' scratch dirs and pytest temp held the files. scripts/tmp_hygiene.py, n8n lane tmp-hygiene (daily 05:00 ET, --plan: manifest only). 2026-10-22: /tmp hit 99% inodes again while the plan-only lane removed nothing; the operator ruled it must delete (auto_apply below). Evaluated: claude_scratch (S), pytest (P), pytest_basetemp (B), named (E), git_trees (G); every other /tmp entry is never a candidate and never scanned. Deletion: scripts/tmp_hygiene_auto.py on host systemd timers under auto_apply.standing_approval (hourly + inode-pressure trigger), or a manual --apply with TRADEAI_DISK_HYGIENE_GRANT; never under the n8n executor (AGENTS.md §24.12 admits only the disk-hygiene lane to n8n deletion; the allowlist never-list keeps destructive retention off n8n).

claude_scratch._why: <root>/<dir_name>/<project>/<session uuid>/: candidate only if idle (newest mtime of the whole tree, bounded scan) > idle_days AND no /proc/*/cwd and no /proc/*/fd inside AND its transcript <transcripts_dir>/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl, when present, is older than transcript_idle_days AND every git tree inside is safe to drop (registered worktrees go through `git worktree remove`, never --force).

pytest._why: <root>/<dir_name>/<entry_glob> (never the pytest-current symlink): candidate if the newest mtime of the tree is older than older_than_days and no cwd / open fd is inside.

pytest_basetemp._why: Rule B (2026-10-22): /tmp/cbd/<pid>/ held 136,419 inodes from `pytest --basetemp=/tmp/cbd/<pid>` runs on 2026-10-21 with fixture mtimes 29 days in the future. <root>/<name> qualifies only when EVERY child is a pid-named real dir; each <pid> dir is a candidate only when it holds nothing but pytest's numbered dirs (<prefix><n>) and <prefix>current symlinks, the pid is not a live pytest/python process, and it is idle > idle_days by its newest real mtime.
pytest_basetemp.creator: ad-hoc `pytest --basetemp=/tmp/<name>/<pid>` runs (agent verification shells); pytest leaves --basetemp trees in place

named._why: Rule E (2026-10-22): top-level /tmp entries whose names a known creator mints; matched by full regex, type pinned, children pinned where the creator's layout is fixed; idle > idle_days, no cwd / open fd. Each rule names its creator so a leak is fixed at source, not only swept.

rules.creator: scripts/pipelines/_manifest_runner.sh step flock, driven by tests/test_pipeline_manifest_runner_20261007.py (worker_/receipt_<hex>) and tests/test_premarket_stage_parallel_20261010.py (par_<hex>); fixed 2026-10-22: the step lock honours PIPELINE_LOCK_DIR
scripts/pipelines/_pipeline_common.sh acquire_lock under the same tests before tests/pipeline_runner_fixtures.runner_env set PIPELINE_LOCK_DIR
scripts/pipelines/_manifest_runner.sh mktemp RESULTS, left behind by every early return (lock busy, safety refusal, corrupt .env); fixed 2026-10-22: removed by a RETURN trap

scripts/lib/hermetic_test_guard.install() fixture (removed by atexit; a killed pytest worker leaks it). Not covered by never_touch_globs tradeai-* (hyphen); the weekly tmp-scratch-cleanup cron archives the >7-day ones it still finds

git_trees._why: Rule G (2026-10-22): top-level /tmp git work trees (agent review worktrees ready-*, candidate-*, pr<N>-*, ... ~13-24k inodes each). Only a registered linked worktree that is clean, unlocked and has no HEAD-only commit (removed by `git worktree remove`, never --force; its branch stays in the main repo), or a clone that is clean with every branch pushed, no stash and no linked worktree left; an unregistered worktree is kept. Idle > idle_days.
git_trees.creator: agent sessions' `git worktree add /tmp/<name>` / `git clone ... /tmp/<name>` review checkouts

scan._why: per-tree bounded lstat walk; a tree the cap stops is never a candidate (idleness unproven)

auto_apply._why: scripts/tmp_hygiene_auto.py on host systemd timers linux_launchers/systemd/tradeai-tmp-hygiene-apply.timer (hourly) and tradeai-tmp-hygiene-pressure.timer (every 5 min; acts only at >= pressure_trigger_pct inode use, at most once per pressure_min_interval_minutes). Fresh plan + apply in one run (re-validation, caps above), deletions ledger + run report + LaneRunReceipt tmp-hygiene-apply. Never the n8n executor: AGENTS.md §24.12 admits only lane disk-hygiene to n8n deletion and the allowlist never-list keeps destructive retention off n8n; n8n keeps the --plan lane and the inode-band monitor. Kill switch: enabled=false (the script then exits without deleting) or stop the timers. Alerts after each run: >= alert_p2_pct P2, >= alert_p1_pct P1 via telegram_alert.send_telegram, deduped by lib/alert_condition_state (system_health:tmp_inodes).

standing_approval.operator: John (repository operator, GitHub PatsKiller), relayed to the agent session 2026-10-22
standing_approval.quote: It needs to be able to delete it. Just looking at it won't do anything.
standing_approval.context: /tmp (tmpfs, 1,048,576 inodes) at 99% inodes on 2026-10-22 (97% on 2026-10-19) while lane tmp-hygiene ran --plan only (22 candidates, 59,088 files reclaimable, nothing removed).
standing_approval.replaces: TRADEAI_DISK_HYGIENE_GRANT on the tmp_hygiene_auto.py path only; a manual scripts/tmp_hygiene.py --apply still needs the grant. Scope: only the tmp rules above (S, P, B, E, G) under never_touch_globs and the home never_touch list; nothing outside /tmp.

monitor._why: scripts/disk_usage_monitor.py, n8n lane disk-usage-monitor (*/15). Band = ok | warn | critical by df-style used% (used / (used + available)). One host comms intent per band CHANGE (dedupe by band, never by raw percent). Inodes (operator 2026-10-19, after /tmp hit 97% inodes with bytes free): every mount is also banded by inode use% (statvfs f_files / f_ffree) with its own thresholds; dedupe is per (mount, metric) band.

inodes._why: inode bands, separate from the byte bands; a filesystem reporting f_files = 0 has no inode limit and is not banded. On an inode alert the summary names the top dirs by file count (bounded scan) for top_dirs.mounts, and the latest tmp_hygiene manifest's reclaimable inodes.
